validator: validator subagent (review-adversarial policy), independent of the session that produced E19 and E24: fresh build, fresh runs, own comparison and own instance checks

repository.working_tree: clean (git status --short empty) at build and at replay start

code_drift: the replay binaries were built from edea86713, not the recorded commits. Over the pipeline path (quartic_folds.rs, klein_v4.rs, d4_weighted_s5.rs, gaudry_quartic.rs, gaudry_quartic_d4.rs, the drivers, Cargo.lock) git diff --stat reports 4,632 insertions and 209 deletions since 4e5810598 and 2,565 insertions and 110 deletions since 854acdbc6 (E25/E26 additions and the report struct's new fields). Every deterministic field of every record nevertheless replays identically, so the drift preserves behaviour on these runs. The fields the newer struct adds (matched_fold, rho_negation_muls, rho_negation_steps) are cross-checked: matched_fold = Negation and the two means equal the committed rho_matched_muls and rho_matched_steps.

environment.host: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz, 4 vCPU, Linux 6.18.44, 15 GiB
environment.determinism_note: collect_and_solve draws each round's targets (2 x rayon threads of them) from the run's single seeded RNG, which also chooses each target's row and feeds Wiedemann, so the thread count is part of the trajectory; the recorded host had 4 vCPUs (rayon default 4) and 4 threads reproduce every record. Field counters are per-instance Cell<u64>, not shared across threads.
environment.concurrency: the E19 stream ran beside the E25 and E24 replays on the same 4 vCPUs for its first part; only wall-clock fields are affected

command: RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4 quartic_pipeline_d4 --sizes P --first-seed S --seeds 1 --rho-runs 16 --json OUT (E19, experiments/27_quartic_pipeline_d4/run_all.sh's arguments, default --max-residuals 200000) and RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4 quartic_pipeline_v4 --sizes P --first-seed S --seeds 1 --rho-runs 16 --max-residuals 5000000 --json OUT (E24, experiments/29_quartic_pipeline_v4/run_all.sh's arguments); OUT in scratch, then copied to replay/e19/ and replay/e24/; replay/replay.sh
comparison: replay/replay_compare.py: every field of every committed record compared with the replay leaf by leaf, integers and floats exactly; wall_ms and solve_ms are wall-clock and are reported, not compared
scalar_verification: For every run the replayed binary recovered x by Wiedemann, checked [x]G = Q by double-and-add on the curve, and set correct = (x == d) for the instance's planted d (quartic_folds.rs Arm::attempt); every replay reports solved = true and correct = true, so x = d on all 22 runs. The committed JSON records correct = true but not x, so x is tied to the committed run through the instance: the replay regenerates it from (p, seed) and its n, #E and h equal the committed ones, and every deterministic counter (targets, decompositions, relations, Wiedemann operations, every walk's steps and F_p multiplications) is identical, which a different instance or a different row system would not give. Independently of the repository code (replay/harness/check_instances.py: own F_{p^4} and curve arithmetic), each regenerated instance satisfies G, Q on E, n prime, [n]G = O, [d]G = Q and #E = h n killing random points, and its j-invariant lies outside F_{p^2}. Each of the 704 walks (16 negation and 16 unfolded per curve) also recovered d (correct = true) and replays identically.
